newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Aokam loan stock downgraded to C1.
newsitem.headline: Aokam loan stock downgraded to C1.

text.p: Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd (RAM) said on Tuesday it has downgraded Aokam Perdana Bhd's 50.6 million ringgit redeemable unsecured loan stock (RULS) to C1 from A2 rating.
In a statement, RAM said the rating indicates "very high risk of default".
"There are factors present that makes the company vulnerable to default. Timely payment of interest and principal is possible only if favourable circumstances continue," the agency said.
It added that the downgrade of the timber company's loan stock reflected the significant deterioration in Aokam's business and financial performance.
RAM said it expects the downtrend continuing "over the immediate term".
"The downgrade also reflects the group's tight liquidity and weak cash flow position," RAM said.
It said other factors considered in the downgrading include the risk associated with the future direction of Aokam in light of uncertainty regarding the group's management and shareholding structure.
